title: draw_drop_markers fade anchors on the NEWEST shed while the doc claims the oldest mark anchors the fade
detail: The doc says the fade is anchored by the oldest mark, but the code tracks the newest tick and fades from it — a bundle shedding at window start and again now renders full alpha. Code and comment disagree.
recommended_fix: Make code and comment agree: either keep `newest` and fix the doc to 'newest mark anchors the fade', or track the group's oldest tick and fade from it.

title: Queue-depth row draws its label unconditionally — dangling 'queue depth (bound N):' when the selected pipe has no bundle
detail: The label is drawn unconditionally; only the E/S/B values are gated on a valid bundle. A selected pipe not on a bundle renders an empty 'queue depth (bound 6):' row — a visible wart the quiet-at-green rule should exclude.
recommended_fix: Draw the label only inside the bundle-valid branch (or draw a placeholder) so the row never shows a label with no values.

title: New pipe_bundle guard checks only the upper bound — ps == -1 indexes pipe_bundle[-1]
detail: The new bounds guard omits ps >= 0. If no pipe is selected (ps == -1) and this code runs, pipe_bundle[-1] is an out-of-bounds panic — the guard's existence implies the author considered invalid ps reachable.
recommended_fix: Guard both sides: `if int(ps) >= 0 && int(ps) < len(app.state.bundles.pipe_bundle)`.

title: Queue-depth row hardcodes 3 lanes with E/S/B labels while every other surface is roster-driven (and the spec says 'BE')
detail: Assumes exactly three lanes E/S/B while the diff elsewhere sizes surfaces to the class roster ('len 8 max') and uses catalog display names — a reordered or grown roster mislabels lanes. The spec matrix's own 'BE n' label also mismatches the impl's 'B'.
recommended_fix: Iterate the roster (or a lane-count constant) with catalog display names instead of hardcoded 3/E/S/B, and align the spec's 'BE' label with the implementation.

title: Drop_Mark.class is written in feed_drop_sites but never read by either draw proc
detail: Both draw procs filter only on reason, bundle, lo/hi and tick; class is stored per mark and never consumed — payload for a display that aggregates per bundle regardless of class.
recommended_fix: Either drop the field or actually use it (color/label markers by class) — storing dead data invites future misuse.

title: Cause-line loop's `int(c) >= len(cat.packet_types)` guard can never fire
detail: counts is allocated with len == len(cat.packet_types) and never resized, so every c in the loop is below len(cat.packet_types) by construction; the guard is unreachable dead code.
recommended_fix: Remove the redundant guard, or size counts independently of the roster if a defensive bound was intended.

title: 'Never overflows the 232 px frame' claim is not guaranteed by capping shown classes at 2
detail: Two long display names plus counts plus '+N more' can still exceed 232 px at 12 pt; the diff itself calls draw_text_c 'byte-truncating', so an overflow clips silently. The cap limits class count, not pixel width.
recommended_fix: Measure the string width (MeasureTextEx, like the QoS row) and truncate on width, or shorten display names — make the claim true by construction.

title: feed_drop_sites runs unconditionally after pp.step — a step that fails without running flow_step re-reads an uncleared scratch
evidence:
pp.step(&app.state, app.tick, {}, &cat) // edits land via the fast-path
				// v2-visibility: copy this tick's drop sites into the presentation
...
				feed_drop_sites(&app)
detail: No error/rejection path appears between pp.step and the feed. Since drop_sites is cleared at flow_step top, a step that returns without running flow_step leaves last tick's sites in the scratch — this feed re-counts them into drop_reasons and re-appends marks.
recommended_fix: Guard the feed on the step actually advancing the sim (clear the scratch in the app loop, or feed only on success).
